verdict.rationale: The vendor says Solo 2 supports the passkey standard with the passkey stored on the key, and the GitHub README says it protects accounts with passkeys/WebAuthn. That implies device-bound discoverable credentials, but the evidence never explicitly documents resident-key storage or the usernameless sign-in flow. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of discoverable/resident credential support, the number of resident-key slots, credential management (listing or deleting individual resident keys), a description of the usernameless sign-in flow, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the key stores discoverable FIDO2 credentials (resident keys / device-bound passkeys) so users can sign in to WebAuthn services without typing a username

citations.quote: Solo 2 supports the passkey standard — except yours stays on your key. Not their cloud.
It's a USB+NFC device that protects your accounts with passkeys/WebAuthn
